title: Serre's criterion for reducedness: reduced iff (R_0) and (S_1)
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Then $R$ is reduced (has no nonzero nilpotent element) if and only if $R$ has properties $(R_0)$ and $(S_1)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk], that is: for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ of height $0$ the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a regular local ring, and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ one has $\operatorname{depth}(R_{\mathfrak p})\ge\min\{1,\dim(R_{\mathfrak p})\}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031R (lemma-criterion-reduced, line 43935), with its proof

proof.text: *Reduced implies $(R_0)$.* Suppose $R$ is reduced. For each height-zero prime $\mathfrak p$, i.e. each minimal prime [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk], the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field]. A field is regular local of dimension zero: its unique maximal ideal is zero, generated by zero elements [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Hence $(R_0)$ holds.

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 031R (lemma-criterion-reduced, lines 43948-43950), citing Lemma Tag 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring)

proof.text: *Reduced implies $(S_1)$.* Fix a prime $\mathfrak p$ and put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If $\dim A=0$, the inequality $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge\min\{1,\dim A\}=0$ is automatic from [def-weil-pbc-depth]. If $\dim A\ge1$, $A$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-preserves-reduced] and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. The maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ cannot equal $\operatorname{Ann}_A(z)$ for any $z\in A$: such a $z$ is nonzero (its annihilator is proper), and cannot be a unit (otherwise $\mathfrak m=0$, so $A$ would be a field of dimension zero); thus $z\in\mathfrak m=\operatorname{Ann}_A(z)$ and $z^2=0$, contrary to reducedness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] to the finite $A$-module $A$ to obtain a nonzerodivisor $t\in\mathfrak m$. The one-term sequence $(t)$ is $A$-regular [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]: multiplication by $t$ is injective and $A/tA\ne0$ since $t$ is a nonunit. Hence $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], which is $(S_1)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk].

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 031R (lemma-criterion-reduced, lines 43950-43957), using Lemma Tag 00LL (lemma-ideal-nonzerodivisor) and Lemma Tag 00LD (lemma-ass-zero-divisors) through the cited nonzerodivisor node

proof.text: *Induction setup and the height-zero case.* Assume $(R_0)$ and $(S_1)$. Every $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and has finite Krull dimension by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]; write this integer as $h(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk]. We prove by induction on $h(\mathfrak p)$ that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is reduced, simultaneously for all primes of each height. If $h(\mathfrak p)=0$, $(R_0)$ makes $R_{\mathfrak p}$ regular local [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk]. By [def-weil-regular-scheme], its maximal ideal can be generated by zero elements and hence is zero; therefore $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field and reduced.

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 031R (lemma-criterion-reduced, lines 43959-43972), base case and induction on prime height

proof.text: *Induction step: regular element and smaller primes.* Let $h(\mathfrak p)=n\ge1$ and suppose $R_{\mathfrak q}$ is reduced for all primes $\mathfrak q$ with $h(\mathfrak q)<n$. Put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Since $\dim A=n$, $(S_1)$ gives $\operatorname{depth}(A)\ge1$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk]. By the definition of depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] there is a one-term $A$-regular sequence $(t)$ in $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], so multiplication by $t$ is injective on $A$. Put $B=A[1/t]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]; the map $A\to B$ is injective because $a/1=0$ means $t^ka=0$ for some $k$, and multiplication by $t^k$ is injective. For any prime $Q\subset B$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] first to $A\to B$ and then to $R\to A$: the contraction $Q'\subset A$ avoids $t$, and its contraction $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ lies strictly below $\mathfrak p$, since $t\in\mathfrak pA$ whereas $t\notin Q'$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localize-localization-at-prime] to $A\to B$ at $Q$ to obtain $B_Q\cong A_{Q'}$, then to $R\to A$ at $Q'$ to obtain $A_{Q'}\cong R_{\mathfrak q}$; their composition gives $B_Q\cong R_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], any chain below $\mathfrak q$ can be extended by $\mathfrak p$; since $h(\mathfrak p)=n$ is finite, $h(\mathfrak q)\le n-1$. Thus $B_Q$ is reduced by the induction hypothesis.

proof.text: *Induction step and conclusion.* All prime localizations $B_Q$ are reduced by Step 4. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-localizations-jointly-injective], $B$ is reduced: a nilpotent $b$ maps to zero in each reduced $B_Q$, hence is zero. The injection $A\hookrightarrow B$ of Step 4 then makes $A$ reduced, since a nilpotent in $A$ maps to a nilpotent, hence zero, in $B$. This finishes the height induction. Every $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is therefore reduced, and another application of [lem-weil-pbc-prime-localizations-jointly-injective] to $R$ shows that $R$ is reduced. Together with Steps 1 and 2 this proves the equivalence.
